target.title: fix(plugins): load newest managed generation when a prior install lingers
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #107228 — after upgrading a long-lived install, a plugin's newly-installed
version can silently fail to take effect: `plugins inspect <id> --runtime` reports
the old version and `install`/`update`/sync appear to no-op.

### Root cause

A managed install/update writes the new version into a distinct managed project
directory (an `__openclaw-generation__` dir) **without removing** the prior flat
project dir. The persisted install-index record keeps pointing at the older,
still-present directory. At load time `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmRecord`
(`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts`) reconciles the persisted
record against a fresh disk scan, but its self-heal branches only cover:

- persisted path **gone** (`isUnavailableManagedNpmInstallRecord`), and
- persisted path **unchanged**, newer version at the *same* path.

The upgrade case — persisted path still present, the same plugin id discovered at
a *different*, newer generation dir — falls through to `return params.persisted`,
so the runtime imports the stale directory.

### Fix

1. **Recover the newest install, not an arbitrary one.**
   `buildRecoveredManagedNpmInstallRecords` previously let whichever project root
   sorted last win for a given plugin id. Generation-dir suffixes are content
   hashes, so on-disk order is unrelated to version. It now folds records through
   `pickNewerRecoveredManagedNpmRecord`, keeping the highest semver across the
   legacy flat dir and every generation dir (ties still prefer the later
   candidate, preserving generation-over-flat behavior).

2. **Repoint to the newer managed install.** When the recovered managed install
   is a strictly newer version at a different path, adopt it — reusing the same
   `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmMetadata(..., { preservePersistedSpec: true })` the
   path-gone branch uses. The repoint is gated on `isManagedNpmInstallPath`, so
   it only applies to persisted records inside the managed npm root; intentional
   custom/outside npm installs are left untouched.

Because this is a recovery-layer self-heal, it also repairs installs that have
**already** diverged from an earlier upgrade, not just future ones.

### Tests

`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-generation-precedence.test.ts`:

- **repoints to a newer managed generation when the persisted install still
  exists** — the upgrade case with the old dir present on disk (not covered by
  `isUnavailableManagedNpmInstallRecord`); asserts `spec`/`resolvedSpec`.
- **adopts the highest version when several generations are present** — pins
  version-based (not sort-order) selection.
- **keeps a current managed install when only an older generation lingers** —
  guard against an older generation superseding a current install.
- **does not repoint an intentional custom npm install outside the managed
  root** — guard for the managed-path gate.

All tests in the file pass; existing recovery/index suites pass.

### Scope / caveats

- **Downgrades are intentionally not auto-adopted.** If a persisted record is
  newer than a lingering directory, the persisted record is kept rather than
  silently downgrading; an explicit downgrade should update the persisted record
  at the install layer.
- This resolves the **load-time symptom** at the recovery layer. If the
  install/update flow should also repoint the persisted record when it writes a
  new generation dir, that is a complementary fix in the install pipeline.
